title: Prove one-disk cutover readiness
goal: Prove one-disk NixOS cutover readiness without performing or device-binding the production cutover: rehearse the exact canonical LUKS2+Btrfs topology from a blank virtual disk, classify all migration-relevant data, establish independently restorable off-host backup capacity and offline recovery material, and finish with a reviewed and evidence-complete cutover plan whose exact production device is deliberately left for a later separately authorized cutover order.

approval.note: This task may prepare and execute disposable virtual-disk rehearsal, classify backup/recovery evidence and produce a reviewed cutover plan. It does not bind a production block device and does not authorize partitioning, mkfs, LUKS/EFI mutation, Secure-Boot or firmware changes, reboot or NixOS switch on the production host.

acceptance.assertion: Starting from a completely blank disposable virtual disk, the exact production-target topology GPT + EFI System Partition + recovery/boot-recovery surface + LUKS2 + Btrfs with @root, @nix, @persist, @home, @data and @containers is created, LUKS unlock is proven, every Btrfs subvolume is mounted correctly, the resulting system actually boots, and independent readback proves the expected topology; the earlier LUKS+ext4 VM proof is not substituted for this gate.

Fresh inventory classifies every migration-relevant non-reproducible data class separately from caches and rebuildable state; current scoped backup success is not treated as proof of complete cutover coverage.

Every critical migration data class has sufficient independent off-host storage and a staged realistic restore test proving representative usable content; a capacity-constrained or non-independently-restorable backup target cannot satisfy this gate.

A fresh disposable system is reconstructed from the reviewed declarative state plus the independently restored non-reproducible data, demonstrating that neither hidden production-host state nor the original system disk is required for recovery.

Independent bootable recovery media plus the required offline host/control closure, source/lock/trust roots and LUKS/recovery material are verified without Grabowski, Bureau, network or the production system SSD.

The cutover plan defines the exact later device-binding procedure and required evidence for model, serial number, mounts, root backing, health and recovery readiness, but deliberately leaves the actual production block-device identity unbound until a separate destructive cutover order freshly authorizes it.

The terminal artifact is a reviewed and evidence-complete one-disk cutover plan binding the approved system closure, exact target topology, point of no return, rollback/reconstruction procedure, mandatory post-boot readback and all prerequisite evidence, while containing no current authorization to execute the production cutover.

This task terminates before sgdisk, wipefs, cryptsetup luksFormat, mkfs, real EFI-partition mutation, Secure-Boot key mutation, firmware write, productive nixos-install, productive switch, or reboot into a new production OS on the Heim-PC; such effects require a later explicit destructive-action approval bound to fresh device and recovery evidence.
All VM/recovery/restore/plan validation and required repository CI are green and the final one-disk plan receives explicit independent review before the task is considered terminal.
